web_title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: Chapter 7: Why MSTX Trades at $8.75 — Implied Expectations vs. Peers
question: What Bitcoin and MSTR path is priced into MSTX at $8.75, and how do its fee, financing, and decay economics compare against MSTR, MSTU, IBIT, BITX, and COIN?

epigraph.quote: Compound interest is the eighth wonder of the world. Negative compounding—paying high financing on a daily-resetting levered bet—is its mirror twin.
epigraph.author: Institutional Derivatives Desk Maxim

web_blocks.html: On November 13, 2026, MSTX closed at $8.75 after its March 19, 2026 1-for-10 reverse split [1, 21]. That price sits -89.47% below its $83.10 TradingView daily-close 52-week high (and -90.77% below its $94.80 intraday 52-week high), marking a -90.60% 1-year loss [21]. MSTX has no earnings multiple, free-cash-flow yield, or EV/EBITDA band. Its share price tracks daily Net Asset Value (NAV), targeting 200% of Strategy Inc. (MSTR) daily returns minus a 1.31% fee and swap financing [1, 2, 21].

To understand why MSTX trades at $8.75, we separate two pricing layers: underlying MSTR valuation and wrapper decay. On November 13, 2026, MSTR closed at $111.62 ($47.14B market cap), well below its 50-day SMA ($143.26) and 200-day SMA ($132.78) [21]. Strategy Inc. holds roughly 850,364 BTC at an average cost near $75,456, while spot Bitcoin trades around $74,000–$75,000 [22, 23]. MSTR's equity trades at an mNAV multiple of 1.09x to 1.20x, down sharply from 2.5x–3.0x+ during 2024–2025 euphoria [22, 23]. That mNAV compression drove roughly half of MSTR's drop, while 2x daily leverage and variance drain compounded MSTX's loss.

web_blocks.title: Reverse-Engineering the Implied Path: What MSTX at $8.75 Assumes

web_blocks.html: A traditional Reverse DCF asks what 10-year revenue growth and operating margin justify today's share price. For a daily-reset 2x leveraged ETF, the equivalent exercise is a Reverse Path-Dependency & Carry Model. Suppose an investor buys MSTX at $8.75 hoping to double their money back to $17.50 over the next 12 months. Because MSTX resets leverage daily at 4:00 PM ET, its 1-year geometric return follows the continuous-time approximation: RMSTX ≈ (1 + RMSTR)2 · exp(-σ2t) - 1 - (Fee + Swap Drag) [1, 5, 19]. Notice what that equation implies: the exponent -σ²t grows with the square of volatility. Doubling underlying volatility quadruples the daily-reset decay rate.

web_blocks.label: 12-Month Reverse Path Requirement to Break Even on Carry & Decay
web_blocks.the_number: +35% to +50% unleveraged MSTR rally needed just to overcome annual volatility drag and financing at 100%+ realized volatility
web_blocks.how_calculated: With MSTX 20-day historical volatility (HV20) and ATM implied volatility at 154.9% (implying MSTR realized volatility ~75%–85%), annual variance drag is roughly sigma_MSTR^2 * t = 0.64 (64% drag in log space), plus 1.31% unitary fee and ~4%–6% net swap financing spread over T-bill collateral yield.
web_blocks.the_inputs: MSTX close $8.75, MSTR close $111.62, HV20 154.9%, unitary ER 1.31%, swap spreads OBFR + 10.00% to +17.00% on 200% notional offset partially by 3.89% T-bill collateral.
web_blocks.the_range: If MSTR ends flat (0%) over 12 months with 75% annualized volatility, MSTX loses roughly -43% to -50% (~$4.40–$5.00). To reach $17.50 (+100%) in a choppy 75%-vol tape, MSTR must gain ~+70% to +85%.
web_blocks.if_off: Only in a low-volatility, monotonic melt-up (where daily moves compound positively with minimal pullback) does 2x daily leverage outperform 2x static leverage.

web_blocks.title: Why 'Cheap Nominal Price ($8.75)' Is a Post-Split Optical Illusion
paragraphs: Retail investors frequently anchor on single-digit share prices, assuming an $8.75 ETF has 'less downside' than a $111.62 stock. In MSTX's case, the $8.75 quote exists only because Tidal Trust II executed a 1-for-10 reverse split on March 19, 2026 [1, 3]. On a split-adjusted basis, MSTX's 52-week high is $83.10, and its 1-year decline is -90.60% [21].

Because MSTX's NAV is purely proportional to daily MSTR moves, there is no intrinsic 'floor' or book-value support at $8.75. If MSTR falls another 35% in a choppy crypto winter, MSTX can lose another 65%–75% and require another reverse split.

web_blocks.html: MSTX also embeds stacked corporate-plus-ETF leverage. Strategy Inc. already uses convertible debt and preferred stock (such as STRC) to finance its 850,364 BTC treasury [22, 23]. With spot Bitcoin near Strategy's ~$75,456 cost basis, MSTR equity behaves like a levered Bitcoin call option. MSTX then layers a 2x daily-resetting swap on top, pushing realized volatility to 154.9% and accelerating mathematical decay [21, 22, 24].

What Would Change Our Valuation Assessment: Only a sustained drop in MSTR realized volatility below 40% combined with fee compression below 1.00% would reduce annual decay; even then, unleveraged MSTR or IBIT (0.25% ER) remains structurally superior for multi-quarter capital [21].

book_paragraphs: When you and I sit down to evaluate an operating business in Chapter 7, we normally ask a simple question: what revenue growth and operating margin is the market's current share price already baking in? With MSTX closing at $8.75 on November 13, 2026, we have to flip that lens on its head. MSTX has no factories, no recurring SaaS customers, and no intrinsic earnings stream. Its $8.75 share price is simply its daily Net Asset Value, and that NAV has collapsed 90.60% over the past twelve months—even after a 1-for-10 reverse split on March 19, 2026 artificially multiplied the nominal quote by ten.

To see why the price is what it is, you have to separate two layers of reality. First, there is Strategy Inc. (MSTR), the underlying equity, which closed at $111.62 with a $47.14 billion market capitalization. With Strategy holding roughly 850,364 Bitcoin at an average cost basis near $75,456 and spot Bitcoin hovering around $74,000 to $75,000 in mid-November 2026, the market has compressed MSTR's mNAV premium down to roughly 1.09x to 1.20x. Gone are the 2024–2025 euphoria multiples where investors paid 2.5x to 3.0x net asset value for Michael Saylor's treasury vehicle. Because MSTR itself is already a leveraged Bitcoin proxy carrying convertible debt and preferred stock, any compression in its mNAV multiple hits the common stock far harder than spot Bitcoin.

Second, and far more lethal for anyone holding MSTX longer than a few trading sessions, is the wrapper-decay layer. When MSTR's 1-year volatility spikes—and right now MSTX's 20-day historical volatility and at-the-money implied volatility sit at an astonishing 154.9%—the mathematics of daily 2x resetting turn into a relentless headwind. Remember the formula we derived in Chapters 2 and 3: every time MSTR swings up 10% on Monday and down 9.1% on Tuesday to finish flat, MSTX rises 20% and falls 18.2%, leaving you down 1.8% in forty-eight hours. Compound that across 252 trading days at 75% to 85% underlying MSTR volatility, add the 1.31% unitary management fee and the OBFR-plus-10%-to-17% total-return swap financing spreads disclosed in the October 31, 2025 Form N-CSRS, and the math becomes unforgiving.

Let's run a Reverse Path Model on $8.75 so you can see the hurdle with your own eyes. Suppose you buy MSTX today at $8.75 hoping to double your money back to $17.50 over the next twelve months. If MSTR simply chops sideways and finishes the year at $111.62—0% return—with 75% annualized volatility, MSTX's variance drag alone wipes out roughly 43% to 50% of your capital, dropping the ETF toward $4.40 to $5.00 before you even count swap carry. To break even at $8.75 over twelve months in a 75%-volatility tape, MSTR has to rally roughly 35% to 50% just to offset the mathematical decay and financing drag. And to double MSTX to $17.50, MSTR needs a 70% to 85% rally unless the move happens in a rare, straight-line melt-up.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Ask yourself: if you wouldn't borrow money at 14% to 21% annualized interest to buy a volatile stock on margin and rebalance your debt every single afternoon at 4:00 PM regardless of price, why would you pay MSTX 1.31% a year to do it for you?

book_subsections.title: The Peer Reality Check: MSTX vs. MSTU, IBIT, and BITX
paragraphs: Look across the peer table as of November 13, 2026, and the structural verdict writes itself. Over the trailing twelve months, spot Bitcoin ETF IBIT—charging just 0.25% on $53.99 billion of assets—fell 32.38%. Even BITX, which uses 2x daily CME Bitcoin futures at a hefty 2.75% expense ratio, fell 66.81%. Meanwhile, MSTX fell 90.60%, virtually identical to its direct 2x MSTR rival MSTU at -90.56%.

Notice two things from that comparison. First, stacking 2x daily ETF leverage on top of MSTR—which already carries corporate debt, convertible notes, and preferred stock leverage against its Bitcoin stack—creates triple-layered volatility that vaporized more than nine-tenths of shareholder capital in a single year. Compare that 58.2-percentage-point underperformance against spot IBIT: an investor who wanted Bitcoin exposure and chose MSTX instead of IBIT lost almost everything in a year when spot Bitcoin was only down a third.

Second, even if a day trader insists on a 2x daily MSTR instrument for an intraday earnings or Bitcoin breakout trade, MSTU charges 1.05% versus MSTX's 1.31% and commands $373.08 million in AUM versus MSTX's $161.65 million. MSTX no longer holds even a fee or scale advantage inside its own niche. In a Reverse Path model, MSTX at $8.75 is not 'cheap'—it is a decaying option-like tracking wrapper whose break-even hurdle over a 12-month choppy tape requires MSTR to rally 35% to 50% just to stand still after variance drag and swap carry. That is why valuation here is not about finding a margin of safety; it is about recognizing negative expected carry.

book_subsections.title: The Post-Split Optical Illusion
paragraphs: One final behavioral trap deserves your attention. When a stock or ETF trades at $8.75, human psychology whispers that it 'can't fall much further'—that $8.75 feels closer to zero than $87.50. Never fall for nominal price anchoring on a reverse-split leveraged ETF. Before March 19, 2026, that $8.75 share was trading at $0.875. There is no book value, no liquidation floor, and no dividend yield supporting $8.75. If MSTR drops another 35% in a choppy crypto downturn, MSTX can easily fall another 65% to $3.00 and trigger yet another 1-for-10 reverse split.

book_subsections.title: Why Stacking Leverage on Top of Corporate Leverage Breaks Compounding
paragraphs: There is one more layer to why $8.75 is not a bargain, and it has nothing to do with Tidal Investments or the swap dealers. It has everything to do with the underlying company itself. Strategy Inc. is not an unlevered software vendor sitting on a pile of cash; it is a leveraged Bitcoin treasury corporation holding 850,364 Bitcoin acquired at an average cost of roughly $75,456 per coin, financed through at-the-market equity issuance, convertible senior notes, and preferred shares. When Bitcoin trades near $74,000 to $75,000, Strategy's equity already carries built-in balance-sheet leverage.

When you buy MSTX, you are putting a 2x daily-resetting total return swap on top of an already levered Bitcoin equity. That is why MSTX's 20-day historical volatility sits at 154.9% while spot Bitcoin ETF IBIT fell only 32.38% over the past year. In good months, the mNAV premium expands from 1.1x toward 2.5x and traders feel invincible; in bad months, mNAV compresses back toward 1.0x while Bitcoin pulls back, hitting MSTR twice and hitting MSTX four times over—all while daily rebalancing locks in the downside math.

book_subsections.title: Why Market Efficiency Doesn't Rescue a Daily-Reset Wrapper
paragraphs: A common pushback I hear from smart investors is: 'If MSTX's decay is so obvious, why doesn't the market price it in?' Here is the subtle truth: the market *does* price it in—not by discounting the NAV below $8.75, because authorized participants arbitrage NAV to fair value every second—but by pricing 154.9% implied volatility into MSTX options and charging OBFR plus 10% to 17% on the underlying swaps.

In other words, institutional market makers and swap desks are never on the losing side of MSTX's math. They hedge their swap books dynamically, collect the OBFR-plus-10%-to-17% financing spread, earn bid-ask spreads on 7 million shares a day, and pass 100% of the path-dependent variance drain directly to the ETF shareholder. That is why no amount of 'cheapness' in MSTR's mNAV multiple turns MSTX into a value investment.
